title: Finite-support cycle reduction in a total resolution
statement: theorem total_resolution_column_zero_cycle_reduction (K : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] (j : K.X 0 ⟶ K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) [∀ i, (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).HasHomology i] [∀ p q, (K.X p).HasHomology q] (n : ℤ) (h_positive : ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero (K.X p)) (hj : ∀ q, j.f q = K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 q q (by simp)) (h_homology : ∀ (p q : ℤ), p < -1 → Function.Exact (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.d p (p + 1)) q).hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.d (p + 1) (p + 2)) q).hom) : ∀ z : (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).cycles n, ∃ y : (K.X 0).cycles n, ∃ b : (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X (n - 1), (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).iCycles n z = j.f n ((K.X 0).iCycles n y) + (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d (n - 1) n b

proof.text: Put A_i = K.X (-i). Represent a total homology class by a cocycle x. The coproduct of modules is their direct sum, so x has finite support. Positive columns vanish, hence x is supported in A_0 through A_r for some natural number r.

If r > 0, the cocycle equations in columns r and r-1 show that x_r is a vertical cycle whose horizontal image is a vertical boundary. Exactness of the horizontal homology row lifts its class to a class in A_(r+1) in vertical degree n+r. Represent that class by a vertical cycle y; its total degree is n-1.

Subtract the total boundary of y, adjusting by the horizontal unit sign, to turn x_r into a vertical boundary. Choose a primitive t in A_r of vertical degree n+r-1 and subtract its appropriately signed total boundary. This kills x_r; the only other column affected is r-1. Induction on r gives a homologous cocycle supported in column zero.

The resulting column-zero component is a vertical cycle y. Sum the finitely many signed correction terms into b in total degree n-1; linearity gives iCycles(z) = j(iCycles(y)) + d(b). The support-zero and zero-cycle cases need no corrections.
